claims.text: Modest Al levels promote local chemical ordering or clustering in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloys.
At modest Al content, the alloy remains a predominantly single-phase fcc matrix.
Configurational entropy stabilizes the single fcc phase at moderate temperatures.
Al-induced ordering produces nanoscale coherent precipitates at internal grain or phase boundaries.
The nanoscale ordered regions obstruct dislocation motion and thereby improve high-temperature strength.
The nanoscale ordered regions act as sinks or traps for radiation-induced defects.
Moderate ordering does not increase stacking-fault energy excessively.
Preserving low stacking-fault energy permits deformation twinning and thereby preserves cryogenic toughness.
A moderate-Al window produces higher high-temperature strength than the low-Al baseline.
A moderate-Al window produces higher radiation resistance than the low-Al baseline by impeding defect migration.
Moderate Al-induced ordering enhances environmental resistance.
A moderate-Al window maintains or improves cryogenic toughness relative to the low-Al baseline.
Excessive Al causes coarse second-phase or precipitate formation.
Coarse second phases produced at excessive Al content reduce cryogenic toughness and ductility.
There is an Al-content threshold above which macroscopic phase separation or full-scale ordering occurs.
The low-Al baseline is a homogeneous fcc solid solution with minimal inhomogeneity.
The controlled comparison varies Al content while retaining fixed ratios among Co, Cr, Fe, and Ni and applying identical thermomechanical processing.
Heat-treatment variables such as cooling rate and aging conditions affect ordered-domain size, distribution, and stacking-fault-energy-related behavior.

contradictions.description: The initial alloy is called equiatomic while also being described as low in Al or having minimal Al addition. A five-component equiatomic alloy contains about 20 at.% Al, so these descriptions are not mutually consistent without a separate definition of 'low Al.'

The intervention says the ratios of the non-Al elements remain constant, whereas the experiment says their elemental concentrations remain fixed. When normalized alloy composition is changed by varying Al, the non-Al ratios can remain fixed, but all their atomic percentages cannot simultaneously remain fixed.
